# Password-reset prototype: prospective risk map

**Stage:** `custom_document` / `acceptance_20261025121757_621df1_risk`  
**Planning task:** T001 (mapping only; the deliverable contract and readable document belong to T002)  
**Identifier range:** `R7B43B-001`–`R7B43B-012`

This is a map of possible delivery failures, **not findings from an implementation review**. No application, tests, or deployment were inspected. Priorities describe the consequence of missing an approved requirement, not measured likelihood: **must** risks directly defeat a security/recovery guarantee or an explicit prohibition; **should** risks impede the required experience, platform fit, or accurate prototype positioning. The proposed checks are future verification, not claims that checks passed.

## Risk items

| Stable ID and risk | Potential failure and impact | Mitigation / acceptance-oriented verification | Priority and rationale | Approved requirement links | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **R7B43B-001 — Sign-in presentation or recovery entry drifts** | The server-rendered sign-in page omits/misrepresents the pictured narrow bordered panel, heading, labeled email field and placeholder, masked password field, underlined recovery link, dark button, or muted footer; or the link does not reach a reset-request form. Users cannot reliably start recovery and the supplied UI is not represented. | Render the sign-in route and inspect its response for pictured visible elements; follow “Forgot password?” and submit an account identifier through the recovery entry. Add pytest coverage for route and entry behavior without inventing sign-in validation or a recovery-page design. | **should** — visible acceptance and entry-point failure, with no evidence that the image specifies broader authentication semantics. | REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-015, REQ-016 | S, I |
| **R7B43B-002 — Reset-request response enumerates accounts** | Existing and unknown account identifiers receive distinguishable visitor-facing results, disclosing account existence. | Submit equivalent requests for a synthetic and an unknown identifier under the same conditions; assert identical visitor-facing response content/status and no disclosure. Keep sink-side issuance checks separate from public response checks. | **must** — directly breaks the ACC-STD-01 non-enumeration guarantee. | REQ-003, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-003 — Per-account request limit can be bypassed** | A sixth request for one account within an hour issues another link, or an elapsed one-hour period remains blocked; abuse protection or legitimate recovery fails. | With controlled time, issue five requests for one synthetic account, attempt a sixth inside the hour and inspect the sink for **no sixth link**; after the applicable hour elapses, verify a new eligible request is not blocked by that prior period. Check per-account behavior rather than imposing an unsupported global limit. | **must** — directly breaks the specified five-per-account-per-hour control. | REQ-004, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-004 — Eligible link is not issued into the prototype sink** | An eligible synthetic-account request has no inspectable reset link, or an unknown identifier creates an account-specific link; recovery becomes unusable or the prototype's account boundary is crossed. | Inspect in-memory notifications after an eligible synthetic-account request for its link and after an unknown-account request for absence of an account-specific link; do not require an external delivery provider. | **must** — recovery cannot complete without a valid link and issue behavior must remain account-scoped. | REQ-005, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-005 — Reset link is reusable** | A consumed link completes a second password change, permitting replay after a legitimate reset. | Complete a reset with an unused link, submit that same link again, and assert no second reset succeeds; test the completed operation rather than assuming that visiting a link consumes it. | **must** — directly breaks ACC-STD-02 single-use protection. | REQ-006, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-006 — Expiry boundary is misinterpreted** | A link works at or after `issued_at + 30 minutes`, or expires before that instant, extending unauthorized access or blocking eligible recovery. | Use controlled time to verify eligibility strictly before `t+30 minutes`, rejection exactly at `t+30 minutes`, and rejection afterward, assuming the link is otherwise valid and unused. | **must** — the exclusive 30-minute boundary is a defined security/acceptance condition. | REQ-007, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-007 — Password replacement does not take effect** | A successful reset leaves the old credential usable or fails to accept the submitted new credential, so the account is not actually recovered. | With a synthetic account and valid unused link, complete a reset; verify the new password is accepted and the old one is not. Do not infer an extra password policy from the story. | **must** — defeats the central recovery outcome. | REQ-008, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-008 — Some active sessions survive a reset** | Invalidation affects only the current session or one device, leaving other authenticated sessions usable after password replacement. | Establish multiple active sessions for one synthetic account; after its successful reset, assert none remains authenticated. Do not prescribe a session implementation. | **must** — directly breaks the ACC-STD-02 all-session sign-out guarantee. | REQ-009, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-009 — Owner notification is omitted or misaddressed** | A successful reset yields no owner-addressed notification, or records it for another account; the owner loses required awareness of the change. | After every successful synthetic-account reset, inspect the in-memory sink for the corresponding owner-addressed successful-reset notification; do not assume external messaging. | **must** — directly breaks ACC-STD-03 notification after success. | REQ-010, REQ-012, REQ-016 | S, K |
| **R7B43B-010 — Runtime, routing, rendering, or tests are incompatible** | The prototype/test suite does not run under Python 3.12, Flask does not serve sign-in and recovery routes, pages require client rendering, or pytest does not exercise the specified scenarios; acceptance cannot be reproduced. | Run application and pytest with declared dependencies on Python 3.12; request sign-in and recovery routes through Flask and inspect server responses for page content. Ensure pytest covers the pictured entry, non-enumeration, request limit, issuance, replay, expiry, credential replacement, all-session sign-out and owner notification. | **should** — delivery cannot be credibly verified in the pinned stack if these fail; behavioral security failures are separately prioritized above. | REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016 | S, I, K |
| **R7B43B-011 — Prototype boundaries are mistaken for production readiness** | Real accounts/external delivery are used instead of synthetic accounts/in-memory notifications, or the documentation omits that these ephemeral substitutes are unsuitable for production. This can misstate safety and make tests dependent on real services. | Exercise only synthetic accounts and inspect sink records without external delivery; document both synthetic accounts and the in-memory sink as production limitations, without treating them as deployable equivalents. | **should** — explicit prototype/documentation fit and honest readiness assessment; no production architecture is requested. | REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-017 | S |
| **R7B43B-012 — Deployment slips into prototype scope** | A deployment action or deployment workflow is introduced despite the explicit no-deployment boundary, increasing exposure beyond the authorized prototype. | Inspect resulting changes and workflow files for absence of deployment additions; perform no deployment action. Keep production-gap documentation descriptive rather than proposing deployment in this run. | **must** — explicit scope prohibition, independent of prototype feature completeness. | REQ-017, REQ-018 | S |

## Coverage and unresolved limits

All approved predecessor identifiers are linked: **REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012, REQ-013, REQ-014, REQ-015, REQ-016, REQ-017, REQ-018**. The links identify affected requirements, not proof of implementation. No extra requirement IDs or stage-output citations are introduced.

- **Assumptions:** The email field supplies the reset account identifier; synthetic accounts and an in-memory notification sink are intentionally ephemeral; controlled time and multiple synthetic sessions may be used in tests; no external delivery, persistence, password policy, or particular session mechanism is specified.
- **Non-blocking questions for later clarification:** Is any sign-in behavior beyond the pictured form required? Are there additional recovery-page or notification presentation requirements? Is a specific session mechanism wanted? Any future production store or delivery provider would require a separately authorized scope.
- **Evidence limit:** The image supports only visible sign-in presentation. S and K support the recovery and prototype boundaries. No implementation or test results establish likelihood, actual defects, or deployment readiness.
